text: Fodor's 'concept nativism', his response to a regress about learning primitive concepts, commits him to the striking claim that:
choices: All concepts are learned by hypothesis-testing from sensory experience
Most concepts, even AIRPLANE, are innate and merely 'triggered' by experience rather than learned from it
Concepts are distributed activation patterns with no discrete identity
Concepts are constituted by their inferential role in a web of belief
explanation: To block a regress in concept learning, Fodor 'bites the bullet': primitive concepts are innate and merely triggered by experience (the concept AIRPLANE was available before airplanes existed), not learned from it. Option 0 is the empiricist learning view Fodor rejects, option 2 is connectionism, and option 3 is inferential/conceptual-role semantics - all rivals to his nativism.
